chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

If a man divorces his wife while he is absent, and she does not know until a year or more or less later, then when she learns of it, she may marry without observing the waiting period (Iddah). And if her husband dies while he is absent, she observes the waiting period from the day the news reaches her, even if he had died a year or two before.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a wife's waiting period if her husband dies or divorces her while he is away?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani clarifies the practical application of Iddah for absent spouses, distinguishing between the immediate eligibility for remarriage upon news of divorce and the requirement to observe the full four-month-ten-day waiting period upon news of death. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that the commencement of the waiting period is tied to the receipt of news (balagh) rather than the actual time of the event, ensuring legal certainty for the wife. This ruling underscores the importance of timely communication in marital jurisprudence within the Imami tradition.
